tier_reason: First-party README and wiki tables only; the GMP side has public code (test/bench_gmp_mt.cpp, built by test/run_bench_gmp_mt.bat with MSVC cl /O2 /openmp against a vcpkg x64-windows gmp.lib), but the TzdLang side is timed by the interpreter's own --bigTime output on a script, the two pages disagree with each other, and the headline CPU ratio leaves out the NTT path's CRT/carry step, so it falls short of A and stays C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README/wiki, 4,741,006-digit operands on i7-4790 + P106-090: CPU AVX2 NTT convolution 54.02 ms vs single-core GMP 6.3.0 mpz_mul 111.78 ms (2.07x as stated); GPU NTT kernel 29.20 ms (3.83x as stated); 8-thread Karatsuba-wrapped GMP 84.58 ms. End-to-end decimal string in to decimal string out: CPU 175.41 ms and GPU 56.52 ms vs single-core GMP 2,549.30 ms (14.5x and 45.1x as stated). The wiki's own breakdown (parse 10.64 + ntt 54.02 + crt_carry 97.08 + format 13.67 ms) shows that the 54.02 ms leaves out CRT reconstruction and carry propagation. The complete CPU product is therefore 151.10 ms, which is 1.35x SLOWER than single-core GMP's 111.78 ms (derived from page data), even though the CPU engine uses OpenMP on all 8 threads. The complete GPU product (ntt=42.01 ms including CRT/carry/copy) is 2.66x faster than single-core GMP (derived from page data). Almost all of the end-to-end gain comes from base-10^9 storage avoiding GMP's binary/decimal conversion (686.85 ms parse + 1,750.67 ms mpz_get_str).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: GMP harness: MSVC cl /O2 /openmp /EHsc /std:c++17 (test/run_bench_gmp_mt.bat), linked against vcpkg x64-windows gmp.lib (whether GMP's assembly kernels were enabled is not stated). TzdTools: MSVC (Visual Studio 2026 / v145) Release via CMakeLists.txt with /arch:AVX2 /openmp; exact optimization flags for the timed build not stated.
corrections.license: MIT (stated only in the README and badge; there is no LICENSE file in the repository: raw main/LICENSE and github.com blob/main/LICENSE both 404)
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers from a 17-day-old language project (first commit 2026-09-13, 81 commits, 10 stars). The NTT multiply is buried in a Windows/MSVC-only interpreter (Generated/TzdExperimentalCompute.cpp uses _umul128; GPU path in TzdPyTorch.cpp) and works on decimal strings. It is not a standalone library. The CPU 2.07x 'pure multiply' ratio compares a multi-threaded NTT convolution that excludes the 97.08 ms CRT/carry step with a complete single-threaded mpz_mul; the complete CPU multiply (151.10 ms) is slower than single-core GMP. The pages contradict each other: the README and CPU wiki give multi-threaded GMP end-to-end as ~519 ms in one place and 2,522.09 ms in the table, and the GPU wiki claims 'over 10x' over GMP for the 29.20 ms kernel (3.83x). The GPU wiki links the benchmark source as a file:/// path on the author's machine. The 'multi-threaded GMP' rows are the author's own Karatsuba split over mpz_mul, not a GMP feature. GMP was a vcpkg MSVC build with unknown asm configuration. Each figure is a single run (iters=1 at 4.74M digits). No LICENSE file (MIT is declared only in the README).

notes: Page numbers match the record, but the page's own phase breakdown undercuts the CPU claim: with CRT/carry included, the AVX2 NTT path takes 151.10 ms and is slower than single-core GMP. Only the GPU path and the decimal-I/O end-to-end case show real wins. Record as shortcomings: not reproducible (single run, inconsistent tables), a misleading ratio, and embedded in an interpreter rather than a library.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed CGO 2018 paper (PDF in the repo, with an artifact appendix) that states compiler (icpc 17.04, -MIC-AVX512 -O3) and CPU (Xeon Phi 7250). Not A, because the MKL baseline harness ships only as a prebuilt binary (solutions_for_comparison/bin; the README says the MKL, CSR-I and ESB sources are withheld), so the benchmark code against the named baseline is not public.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Paper (CGO 2018, PDF in repo): on scale-free matrices CVR is up to 40x (2.84x on average) faster than MKL and up to 1.70x (1.33x on average) faster than the best existing approach. On HPC matrices it is up to 17x (1.22x on average in the introduction, 1.24x in Section 7.1) faster than MKL and up to 1.57x (1.10x on average) faster than the best existing approach. Peak per-matrix ratios over MKL: wiki-talk 39.53x, ins2 17.58x. Table 3 domain averages, GFlop/s CVR vs MKL: web graph 7.28 vs 2.92, routing 17.11 vs 2.73, road 9.57 vs 4.24.
corrections.caveats: Peer-reviewed with a public CVR artifact (spmv.cpp, Makefile, run scripts), but the MKL, CSR(I) and ESB comparison programs are binaries only (the authors withheld the sources over licensing), so the baseline side cannot be inspected or rebuilt. The code supports only Knights Landing (AVX-512 MIC, icpc 17, MCDRAM in flat mode), which Intel discontinued, so the numbers cannot be reproduced on current hardware without porting. Numbers are the authors' own; the best SMT thread count and parameters were picked per method. The intro (1.22x) and Section 7.1 (1.24x) disagree on the HPC average over MKL. The README contains no numbers. MKL is not one of SuiteSparse, Eigen sparse or PETSc. Dormant since August 2018 apart from a February 2024 README edit.

notes: Numbers verified in the paper PDF (abstract, Section 1, Table 3, Section 7.1). Downgraded A to B only because the MKL baseline harness is binary-only. Metadata confirmed: MIT, 24 stars, not a fork, last commit 2024-02-12 (stale).

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed (Future Generation Computer Systems 116, 2021) speedups vs MKL, CSR5 and Merge are quoted in the README's abstract. ALBUS code and Makefiles are public, but the harnesses for MKL, CSR5 and Merge are not in the repo, and the MKL column of the README table is empty, so it falls short of A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Both Makefiles (ALBUS(OpenMP) and ALBUS(OpenMP+AVX2)): icpc -g -w -fno-alias -qopt-report -qopt-report-phase=all -mbranches-within-32B-boundaries -falign-double -inline-calloc -falign-loops=8 -xCORE-AVX2 -fopenmp -O3. The README's example shows an older 'icpc -xCORE-AVX2 -qopt-prefetch=3 -fopenmp -O3'. A commented g++ alternative uses -march=native -mavx -mavx2 -fopenmp -O3. The icpc version is not stated.
corrections.hardware: README table: dual-socket Intel Xeon Gold 6242 (2x16 cores). Abstract numbers: dual-socket Xeon E5-2670 v3. The README also lists a dual-socket Xeon Silver 4110 test platform.
corrections.caveats: Peer-reviewed paper but the authors' own benchmark. The MKL column of the README table is empty, so the MKL ratios appear only in the paper abstract (the paper itself was not reachable: sciencedirect.com is blocked here). The README table (Xeon Gold 6242) and the abstract (E5-2670 v3) use different CPUs. ALBUS loses to CVR on cant, ins2 and pdb1HYS in the README table. main.cpp runs the albus_balance preprocessing outside the timed loop, after a warm-up of the same number of iterations, so the GFlops exclude preprocessing. No comparison harness for MKL, CSR5 or Merge is in the repo. MKL is not one of SuiteSparse, Eigen sparse or PETSc. Hardware is 2014-2019 era and the repo has been idle since April 2022 (README edits).

notes: README numbers and abstract ratios match the record exactly. Fixed the flags (the actual Makefiles differ from the README's example) and noted that preprocessing is excluded from the timing. Metadata confirmed: MIT, 17 stars, not a fork, last commit 2022-04-04 (abandoned, >3 years before today).
